200.description: The updated tenant, in the same shape as `GET /tenants/{tenant}`. `meta.warnings` is always present: a `phone_number_shared` entry means the write applied but another account answers on that number (`tenant_ids` lists the ones your token can see); an `external_tenant_id_cutover` entry means the re-key applied but your account still has an inbound PMS sync that could re-create the old id.

403.description: Your token does not carry the `tenants:write` scope.

404.description: No tenant with that `tenant_id` at a location your token reaches.

409.description: The tenant exists but cannot be updated here. `code` is `tenant_not_externally_linked` when the account carries no id from your system, `tenant_profile_ambiguous` when your token reaches more than one of the tenant's records, `tenant_spans_locations` when a name was sent for a tenant holding records at several of your locations, or when a re-key was sent but your token does not reach every location the tenant occupies (identity and name are each one value behind all of them; a phone number is held per location, so sending that alone still works), or `external_tenant_id_conflict` when the `external_tenant_id` you sent already belongs to another tenant in your account.

422.description: No writable field was sent, or the phone number could not be read. Sending any field other than `first_name`, `last_name`, `phone`, or `external_tenant_id` also answers `422`, with the reason keyed by field name: `email`, `location_id`, `is_secondary`, `is_classified`, `access_start_time`, `access_end_time`, `access_hours`, and `archived_at` are all owned elsewhere.

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
